subject: plutonium core
title: A Plutonium Ball Killed Two Scientists. One Slip of a Screwdriver

scenes.text: A 14-pound ball of plutonium killed two scientists, one at a time.
Los Alamos, August 1945. Harry Daghlian was stacking tungsten bricks around the core when one slipped and landed on it. A blue glow, a wave of heat. He died 25 days later.
May 1946. Louis Slotin lowered a beryllium dome over the same core, holding the gap open with the tip of a screwdriver. It slipped.
A blue flash. He flipped the dome off with his bare hand within a second, protecting the men beside him. He'd taken close to 1,000 rads. Nine days later he was dead.
Richard Feynman called these experiments tickling the tail of a sleeping dragon.
At Los Alamos the sphere got a nickname that stuck: the demon core.

description:
One 6.2-kilogram sphere of plutonium killed two Los Alamos scientists in two separate criticality accidents, nine months apart.
On 21 August 1945 Harry Daghlian dropped a tungsten carbide brick onto the core, saw a blue glow and felt a wave of heat, and died 25 days later. On 21 May 1946 Louis Slotin was lowering a beryllium hemisphere over the same core, using a screwdriver to hold the gap, when it slipped; there was a blue flash, he flipped the shell off by hand, and he died nine days later after a dose of close to 1,000 rads. Richard Feynman compared the experiments to tickling the tail of a sleeping dragon. The sphere became known as the demon core.
Would you have taken that job?
first_comment: Two deaths, nine months apart, from the same 14-pound sphere. Would you have picked up that screwdriver?
